sources.title: Repository source boundary for transaction-chain sync/async tradeoff
Transactional outbox pattern - AWS Prescriptive Guidance
Apache Kafka 4.1 Design - message delivery semantics and transactions

claims.text: The repository source asks for sync/async boundary selection in a transaction chain and the UX/write-performance tradeoff, but preserves no production topology, SLO, QPS, mandatory middleware, or company-specific implementation.

Transactional outbox addresses the dual-write gap between a database state change and event publication by persisting the business update and outbox record in one local transaction, with later publication; consumers still need idempotence because duplicate delivery can occur.
Long-lived multi-service transactions can use Saga-style state transitions and compensating actions rather than pretending one local database transaction spans independent services.

Kafka documents at-most-once, at-least-once and exactly-once scopes; producer idempotence/transactions have bounded guarantees and do not by themselves make arbitrary external side effects exactly-once.
The recovery-capacity inequality mu_recovery > lambda + B/T is an explicit queue-drain derivation from arrival rate, backlog and desired drain time, not a repository-source fact or vendor threshold.
